Data:Weather.clouds.json.label: Clouds
Data:Weather.clouds.json.desc: In this country the sky is rarely clear. The Sun goes courteously cloaked.

Data:Weather.earthquake.json.label: Earthquake
Data:Weather.earthquake.json.desc: The gentlest of earth tremors. Just to remind us that the earth is not dead but sleeping.

Data:Weather.enactor.numa.json.label: Nume-Brume
Data:Weather.enactor.numa.json.comments: This works differently from all the other enactors. It's called directly from the numa-begin recipe (below) in order to output the numa weather, because of escapement issues; and it's numa-begin that calls the fx. The convention is kept for the name so we don't break legacy saves - so we have a season.numa req to prevent it from firing when every other season calls a wildcard weather enactor.

Data:Weather.gale.json.label: Gale
Data:Weather.gale.json.desc: Trees bend, walls creak, travellers bend low against the blast.

Data:Weather.hail.json.label: Hail
Data:Weather.hail.json.desc: Ice raps on the roofs and tree-tops.

Data:Weather.json.label: Weather
Data:Weather.json.desc: Each kind of weather brings its own influence. I can make use of these as a Memory.

Data:Weather.snow.json.label: Snow
Data:Weather.snow.json.desc: The world is pale today. 'The White is west of the world, and winter does not wait forever', Solomon Husher once said.

Data:Weather.sunny.json.label: Sunny
Data:Weather.sunny.json.desc: The Sun is not what it was, but today he is smiling.

Data:Well.renounce.journal.json.label: Renounce What Could Be
Data:Well.renounce.journal.json.startdescription: Do I really want to fling my journal into the well? [THIS WILL DESTROY YOUR JOURNAL, which will make it IMPOSSIBLE TO COMPLETE THE GAME. You'll be stuck! But you can do it if you really want.]
Data:Well.renounce.journal.json.desc: 'Fool of a Librarian!' [It is no longer possible to complete the game.]

Data:Well.renounce.json.label: Renounce
Data:Well.renounce.json.startdescription: If I drop an object into the well, I'm unlikely to see it again. [Use this to dispose of junk, or of danger.]

Data:Well.renounce.penny.json.label: Renounce
Data:Well.renounce.penny.json.startdescription: The smallest of wishes. [Dispose of a stray penny.]

Data:Whip.prune.json.Label: Prune Whip
Data:Whip.prune.json.Desc: Much, much tastier than it sounds.

Data:Whispering.sand.json.Label: Whispering Sand
Data:Whispering.sand.json.Desc: White-silver sand in which the voice of the waves lingers...

xexts.scrutiny: The voice of the waves lingers no longer.

Data:Windinwaiting.json.Label: Wind-in-Waiting
Data:Windinwaiting.json.Desc: 'When the sun was redder, when the world was softer, and the Thirty ruled the sky… the winds were better neighbours.'

Data:Window.madrugad.json.Label: Stained Glass Window: the Madrugad
Data:Window.madrugad.json.Desc: THAT WHICH IS NOT NEEDED, THAT SHALL BE QUENCHED

Data:Window.meniscate.json.Label: Stained Glass Window: the Meniscate
Data:Window.meniscate.json.Desc: WHAT IS WITHIN, WITHOUT; WHAT IS WITHOUT, WITHIN

Data:Window.suninrags.json.Label: Stained Glass Window: the Sun-in-Rags
Data:Window.suninrags.json.Desc: WHEN IT ENDS, IT WILL BE A BEAUTIFUL ENDING

Data:Window.watchman.json.Label: Stained Glass Window: the Watchman
Data:Window.watchman.json.Desc: THE WAY IS LIT FOR THE WILLING AND FOR THE UNWILLING

Data:Windrumour.json.Label: Wind-Rumour
Data:Windrumour.json.Desc: 'If the cloud were a canvas, who spread it? If the sky were a sheet, who knotted it?' A Wind-Rumour is an auspice found in the sky by those who look too long, interpretable only by the wise.

Data:Wings.grail.json.Label: Lepidoptery Display (Grail-centric)
Data:Wings.grail.json.Desc: A collection of lepidopteran insects with unusual characteristics.

xexts.scrutiny: On closer inspection, these are more like bees, but they seem to have adopted the wings and limbs of other insects, rather like hermit crabs. A typed card reads PROPINOMANIDAE.

Data:Wings.heart.json.Label: Lepidoptery Display (Heart-centric)
Data:Wings.heart.json.Desc: A collection of lepidopteran insects with unusual characteristics.

xexts.scrutiny: The bulbous heads of these insects are alarmingly well-endowed with a great many eyes. A typed card reads TRIGINTIDAE.

Data:Wings.moth.json.Label: Lepidoptery Display (Moth-centric)
Data:Wings.moth.json.Desc: A collection of lepidopteran insects with unusual characteristics.

xexts.scrutiny: The wings of these insects shimmer darkly as the light shifts. A typed card reads FULGENIDAE.
